overview:
This check monitors [ClickHouse][1] through the Datadog Agent.

Enable [Database Monitoring][11] (DBM) for enhanced insights into query performance and database health. In addition to the standard integration, Datadog DBM provides query-level metrics, live and historical query snapshots, query explain plans, query errors, and parts and merges observability.

**Note**: Database Monitoring for ClickHouse is in Preview and requires Datadog Agent v7.78 or later. Customers who participate in the preview will not be charged for usage incurred during the preview period.

**Minimum Agent version:** 7.16.0

[1]: https://clickhouse.com/
[11]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/database_monitoring/setup_clickhouse/
setup:
> **Note:** This page describes the standard ClickHouse Agent integration. If you are looking for the Database Monitoring product for ClickHouse, see [Database Monitoring for ClickHouse](https://docs.datadoghq.com/database_monitoring/setup_clickhouse/).

Follow the instructions below to install and configure this check for an Agent running on a host. For containerized environments, see the [Autodiscovery Integration Templates][2] for guidance on applying these instructions.

### Installation

The ClickHouse check is included in the [Datadog Agent][3] package. No additional installation is needed on your server.

### Configuration

#### Prepare ClickHouse

As a best practice, Datadog recommends using a read-only user to monitor your ClickHouse instance. This limits the access granted to the Datadog Agent.

<!-- xxx tabs xxx -->
<!-- xxx tab "Host" xxx -->

#### Host

To configure this check for an Agent running on a host:

#### Metric collection

1. To start collecting your ClickHouse performance data, edit the `clickhouse.d/conf.yaml` file in the `conf.d/` folder at the root of your Agent's configuration directory. See the [sample clickhouse.d/conf.yaml][4] for all available configuration options.

*Note*: This integration uses the official `clickhouse-connect` client to connect over HTTP.

*Note*: If your ClickHouse Cloud service sits behind a single load-balanced endpoint, set `single_endpoint_mode: true`. This tells the Agent (version 7.83.0 or later) to query system-table metrics across all nodes behind that endpoint using `clusterAllReplicas()`, tagging each resulting series with `clickhouse_node` so you can still distinguish per-node data.

Without this setting, the Agent may hit a different node on each collection cycle. For cumulative per-node counters like `clickhouse.query.failed.count`, that inconsistency produces inaccurate values, since the counter isn't being read from the same source each time.

2. [Restart the Agent][5].

##### Log collection

1. Collecting logs is disabled by default in the Datadog Agent, enable it in your `datadog.yaml` file:

   ```yaml
   logs_enabled: true
   ```

2. Add the log files you are interested in to your `clickhouse.d/conf.yaml` file to start collecting your ClickHouse logs:

   ```yaml
     logs:
       - type: file
         path: /var/log/clickhouse-server/clickhouse-server.log
         source: clickhouse
         service: "<SERVICE_NAME>"
   ```

    Change the `path` and `service` parameter values and configure them for your environment. See the [sample clickhouse.d/conf.yaml][4] for all available configuration options.

3. [Restart the Agent][5].

<!-- xxz tab xxx -->
<!-- xxx tab "Containerized" xxx -->

#### Containerized

For containerized environments, see the [Autodiscovery Integration Templates][2] for guidance on applying the parameters below.

#### Metric collection

| Parameter            | Value                                                      |
|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| `<INTEGRATION_NAME>` | `clickhouse`                                                   |
| `<INIT_CONFIG>`      | blank or `{}`                                              |
| `<INSTANCE_CONFIG>`  | `{"server": "%%host%%", "port": "%%port%%", "username": "<USER>", "password": "<PASSWORD>"}`       |

##### Log collection

Collecting logs is disabled by default in the Datadog Agent. To enable it, see [Kubernetes log collection][6].

| Parameter      | Value                                     |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------|
| `<LOG_CONFIG>` | `{"source": "clickhouse", "service": "<SERVICE_NAME>"}` |

<!-- xxz tab xxx -->
<!-- xxz tabs xxx -->

### Validation

[Run the Agent's status subcommand][7] and look for `clickhouse` under the **Checks** section.

metrics.name: clickhouse.CompiledExpressionCacheCount
metrics.description: Total entries in the cache of JIT-compiled code.

metrics.name: clickhouse.MarkCacheFiles
metrics.description: The number of mark files cached in the mark cache.

metrics.name: clickhouse.ReplicasMaxInsertsInQueue
metrics.description: Maximum number of INSERT operations in the queue (still to be replicated) across Replicated tables.

metrics.name: clickhouse.ReplicasMaxMergesInQueue
metrics.description: Maximum number of merge operations in the queue (still to be applied) across Replicated tables.

metrics.name: clickhouse.ReplicasMaxQueueSize
metrics.description: Maximum queue size (in the number of operations like get, merge) across Replicated tables.

metrics.name: clickhouse.ReplicasSumInsertsInQueue
metrics.description: Sum of INSERT operations in the queue (still to be replicated) across Replicated tables.

metrics.name: clickhouse.ReplicasSumMergesInQueue

metrics.name: clickhouse.UncompressedCacheBytes
metrics.description: Total size of uncompressed cache in bytes. Uncompressed cache does not usually improve the performance and should be mostly avoided.

metrics.name: clickhouse.UncompressedCacheCells
metrics.description: Total number of entries in the uncompressed cache. Each entry represents a decompressed block of data. Uncompressed cache does not usually improve performance and should be mostly avoided.

metrics.name: clickhouse.addresses.active

metrics.name: clickhouse.aggregator.threads

metrics.name: clickhouse.aggregator.threads.active
metrics.description: Number of threads in the Aggregator thread pool running a task.

metrics.name: clickhouse.aggregator.threads.scheduled
metrics.description: Number of queued or active jobs in the Aggregator thread pool.

metrics.name: clickhouse.aio.read.count
metrics.description: Number of reads with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface.

metrics.name: clickhouse.aio.read.size.count
metrics.description: Number of bytes read with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface.

metrics.name: clickhouse.aio.read.size.total

metrics.name: clickhouse.aio.read.total
metrics.description: Total number of reads with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface.

metrics.name: clickhouse.aio.write.count
metrics.description: Number of writes with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface.

metrics.name: clickhouse.aio.write.size.count
metrics.description: Number of bytes read with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface.

metrics.name: clickhouse.aio.write.size.total
metrics.description: Total number of bytes read with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface.

metrics.name: clickhouse.aio.write.total
metrics.description: Total number of writes with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface.

metrics.name: clickhouse.async.read.time
metrics.description: Time spent in waiting for asynchronous reads in asynchronous local read.

metrics.name: clickhouse.async.reader.ignored.bytes.count
metrics.description: Number of bytes ignored during asynchronous reading

metrics.name: clickhouse.async.reader.ignored.bytes.total
metrics.description: Number of bytes ignored during asynchronous reading

metrics.name: clickhouse.async.remote_read.time
metrics.description: Time spent in waiting for asynchronous remote reads.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.AsynchronousHeavyMetricsCalculationTimeSpent
metrics.description: Time in seconds spent for calculation of asynchronous heavy (tables related) metrics (this is the overhead of asynchronous metrics).

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.AsynchronousHeavyMetricsUpdateInterval
metrics.description: Heavy (tables related) metrics update interval

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.AsynchronousMetricsCalculationTimeSpent
metrics.description: Time in seconds spent for calculation of asynchronous metrics (this is the overhead of asynchronous metrics).

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.AsynchronousMetricsUpdateInterval
metrics.description: Metrics update interval

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.CGroupMaxCPU
metrics.description: The maximum number of CPU cores according to CGroups.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.CGroupMemoryTotal
metrics.description: The total amount of memory in cgroup, in bytes. If stated zero, the limit is the same as OSMemoryTotal.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.CGroupMemoryUsed
metrics.description: The amount of memory used in cgroup, in bytes.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.CGroupSystemTime
metrics.description: The ratio of time the CPU core was running OS kernel (system) code.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.CGroupSystemTimeNormalized
metrics.description: The value is similar to `CGroupSystemTime` but divided by the number of available CPU cores to be measured in the [0..1] interval regardless of the number of cores. This allows you to average the values of this metric across multiple servers in a cluster even if the number of cores is non-uniform, and still get the average resource utilization metric.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.CGroupUserTime
metrics.description: The ratio of time the CPU core was running userspace code. This includes also the time when the CPU was under-utilized due to the reasons internal to the CPU (memory loads, pipeline stalls, branch mispredictions, running another SMT core).

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.CGroupUserTimeNormalized
metrics.description: The value is similar to `CGroupUserTime` but divided by the number of available CPU cores to be measured in the [0..1] interval regardless of the number of cores. This allows you to average the values of this metric across multiple servers in a cluster even if the number of cores is non-uniform, and still get the average resource utilization metric.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.CompiledExpressionCacheBytes
metrics.description: Total bytes used for the cache of JIT-compiled code.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.CompiledExpressionCacheCount
metrics.description: Total entries in the cache of JIT-compiled code.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.DictionaryTotalFailedUpdates
metrics.description: Sum of sequantially failed updates in all dictionaries

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.FilesystemCacheBytes
metrics.description: Total bytes in the `cache` virtual filesystem. This cache is hold on disk.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.FilesystemCacheCapacity
metrics.description: Total capacity in the `cache` virtual filesystem. This cache is hold on disk.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.FilesystemCacheFiles
metrics.description: Total number of cached file segments in the `cache` virtual filesystem. This cache is hold on disk.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.FilesystemLogsPathAvailableBytes
metrics.description: Available bytes on the volume where ClickHouse logs path is mounted. If this value approaches zero, you should tune the log rotation in the configuration file.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.FilesystemLogsPathAvailableINodes
metrics.description: The number of available inodes on the volume where ClickHouse logs path is mounted.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.FilesystemLogsPathTotalBytes
metrics.description: The size of the volume where ClickHouse logs path is mounted, in bytes. It's recommended to have at least 10 GB for logs.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.FilesystemLogsPathTotalINodes
metrics.description: The total number of inodes on the volume where ClickHouse logs path is mounted.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.FilesystemLogsPathUsedBytes
metrics.description: Used bytes on the volume where ClickHouse logs path is mounted.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.FilesystemLogsPathUsedINodes
metrics.description: The number of used inodes on the volume where ClickHouse logs path is mounted.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.FilesystemMainPathAvailableBytes
metrics.description: Available bytes on the volume where the main ClickHouse path is mounted.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.FilesystemMainPathAvailableINodes
metrics.description: The number of available inodes on the volume where the main ClickHouse path is mounted. If it is close to zero, it indicates a misconfiguration, and you will get 'no space left on device' even when the disk is not full.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.FilesystemMainPathTotalBytes
metrics.description: The size of the volume where the main ClickHouse path is mounted, in bytes.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.FilesystemMainPathTotalINodes
metrics.description: The total number of inodes on the volume where the main ClickHouse path is mounted. If it is less than 25 million, it indicates a misconfiguration.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.FilesystemMainPathUsedBytes
metrics.description: Used bytes on the volume where the main ClickHouse path is mounted.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.FilesystemMainPathUsedINodes
metrics.description: The number of used inodes on the volume where the main ClickHouse path is mounted. This value mostly corresponds to the number of files.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.HashTableStatsCacheEntries
metrics.description: The number of entries in the cache of hash table sizes. The cache for hash table sizes is used for predictive optimization of GROUP BY.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.HashTableStatsCacheHits
metrics.description: The number of times the prediction of a hash table size was correct.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.HashTableStatsCacheMisses
metrics.description: The number of times the prediction of a hash table size was incorrect.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.IndexMarkCacheBytes
metrics.description: Total size of mark cache for secondary indices in bytes.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.IndexMarkCacheFiles
metrics.description: Total number of mark files cached in the mark cache for secondary indices.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.IndexUncompressedCacheBytes
metrics.description: Total size of uncompressed cache in bytes for secondary indices. Uncompressed cache does not usually improve the performance and should be mostly avoided.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.IndexUncompressedCacheCells
metrics.description: Total number of entries in the uncompressed cache for secondary indices. Each entry represents a decompressed block of data. Uncompressed cache does not usually improve performance and should be mostly avoided.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.Jitter
metrics.description: The difference in time the thread for calculation of the asynchronous metrics was scheduled to wake up and the time it was in fact, woken up. A proxy-indicator of overall system latency and responsiveness.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.LoadAverage1
metrics.description: The whole system load, averaged with exponential smoothing over 1 minute.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.LoadAverage15
metrics.description: The whole system load, averaged with exponential smoothing over 15 minutes.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.LoadAverage5
metrics.description: The whole system load, averaged with exponential smoothing over 5 minutes.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.MMapCacheCells
metrics.description: The number of files opened with `mmap` (mapped in memory). This is used for queries with the setting `local_filesystem_read_method` set to `mmap`. The files opened with `mmap` are kept in the cache to avoid costly TLB flushes.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.MarkCacheBytes
metrics.description: Total size of mark cache in bytes

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.MarkCacheFiles
metrics.description: Total number of mark files cached in the mark cache

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.MaxPartCountForPartition
metrics.description: Maximum number of parts per partition across all partitions of all tables of MergeTree family. Values larger than 300 indicates misconfiguration, overload, or massive data loading.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.MemoryCode
metrics.description: The amount of virtual memory mapped for the pages of machine code of the server process, in bytes.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.MemoryDataAndStack
metrics.description: The amount of virtual memory mapped for the use of stack and for the allocated memory, in bytes. It is unspecified whether it includes the per-thread stacks and most of the allocated memory, that is allocated with the 'mmap' system call. This metric exists only for completeness reasons. I recommend to use the `MemoryResident` metric for monitoring.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.MemoryResident
metrics.description: The amount of physical memory used by the server process, in bytes.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.MemoryResidentMax
metrics.description: Maximum amount of physical memory used by the server process, in bytes.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.MemoryShared
metrics.description: The amount of memory used by the server process, that is also shared by another processes, in bytes. ClickHouse does not use shared memory, but some memory can be labeled by OS as shared for its own reasons. This metric does not make a lot of sense to watch, and it exists only for completeness reasons.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.MemoryVirtual
metrics.description: The size of the virtual address space allocated by the server process, in bytes. The size of the virtual address space is usually much greater than the physical memory consumption, and should not be used as an estimate for the memory consumption. The large values of this metric are totally normal, and makes only technical sense.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.NetworkTCPReceiveQueue
metrics.description: Total size of receive queues of network sockets used on the server across TCPv4 and TCPv6.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.NetworkTCPSocketRemoteAddresses
metrics.description: Total number of unique remote addresses of network sockets used on the server across TCPv4 and TCPv6.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.NetworkTCPSockets
metrics.description: Total number of network sockets used on the server across TCPv4 and TCPv6, in all states.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.NetworkTCPTransmitQueue
metrics.description: Total size of transmit queues of network sockets used on the server across TCPv4 and TCPv6.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.NetworkTCPUnrecoveredRetransmits
metrics.description: Total size of current retransmits (unrecovered at this moment) of network sockets used on the server across TCPv4 and TCPv6.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.NumberOfDatabases
metrics.description: Total number of databases on the server.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.NumberOfDetachedByUserParts
metrics.description: The total number of parts detached from MergeTree tables by users with the `ALTER TABLE DETACH` query (as opposed to unexpected, broken or ignored parts). The server does not care about detached parts and they can be removed.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.NumberOfDetachedParts
metrics.description: The total number of parts detached from MergeTree tables. A part can be detached by a user with the `ALTER TABLE DETACH` query or by the server itself it the part is broken, unexpected or unneeded. The server does not care about detached parts and they can be removed.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.NumberOfPendingMutations
metrics.description: The total number of mutations that are in left to be mutated.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.NumberOfPendingMutationsOverExecutionTime
metrics.description: The total number of mutations which have data part left to be mutated over the specified max_pending_mutations_execution_time_to_warn setting.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.NumberOfStuckMutations
metrics.description: The total number of mutations which have data part left to be mutated over the last 1 hour.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.NumberOfTables
metrics.description: Total number of tables summed across the databases on the server, excluding the databases that cannot contain MergeTree tables. The excluded database engines are those who generate the set of tables on the fly, like `Lazy`, `MySQL`, `PostgreSQL`, `SQlite`.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.NumberOfTablesSystem
metrics.description: Total number of tables in the system database on the server stored in tables of MergeTree family.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSCPUOverload
metrics.description: Relative CPU deficit, calculated as: how many threads are waiting for CPU relative to the number of threads, using CPU. If it is greater than zero, the server would benefit from more CPU. If it is significantly greater than zero, the server could become unresponsive. The metric is accumulated between the updates of asynchronous metrics.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSContextSwitches
metrics.description: The number of context switches that the system underwent on the host machine. This is a system-wide metric, it includes all the processes on the host machine, not just clickhouse-server.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSGuestNiceTimeNormalized
metrics.description: The value is similar to `OSGuestNiceTime` but divided to the number of CPU cores to be measured in the [0..1] interval regardless of the number of cores. This allows you to average the values of this metric across multiple servers in a cluster even if the number of cores is non-uniform, and still get the average resource utilization metric.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSGuestTimeNormalized
metrics.description: The value is similar to `OSGuestTime` but divided to the number of CPU cores to be measured in the [0..1] interval regardless of the number of cores. This allows you to average the values of this metric across multiple servers in a cluster even if the number of cores is non-uniform, and still get the average resource utilization metric.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSIOWaitTimeNormalized
metrics.description: The value is similar to `OSIOWaitTime` but divided to the number of CPU cores to be measured in the [0..1] interval regardless of the number of cores. This allows you to average the values of this metric across multiple servers in a cluster even if the number of cores is non-uniform, and still get the average resource utilization metric.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSIdleTimeNormalized
metrics.description: The value is similar to `OSIdleTime` but divided to the number of CPU cores to be measured in the [0..1] interval regardless of the number of cores. This allows you to average the values of this metric across multiple servers in a cluster even if the number of cores is non-uniform, and still get the average resource utilization metric.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSInterrupts
metrics.description: The number of interrupts on the host machine. This is a system-wide metric, it includes all the processes on the host machine, not just clickhouse-server.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSIrqTimeNormalized
metrics.description: The value is similar to `OSIrqTime` but divided to the number of CPU cores to be measured in the [0..1] interval regardless of the number of cores. This allows you to average the values of this metric across multiple servers in a cluster even if the number of cores is non-uniform, and still get the average resource utilization metric.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSMemoryAvailable
metrics.description: The amount of memory available to be used by programs, in bytes. This is very similar to the `OSMemoryFreePlusCached` metric. This is a system-wide metric, it includes all the processes on the host machine, not just clickhouse-server.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSMemoryBuffers
metrics.description: The amount of memory used by OS kernel buffers, in bytes. This should be typically small, and large values may indicate a misconfiguration of the OS. This is a system-wide metric, it includes all the processes on the host machine, not just clickhouse-server.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSMemoryCached
metrics.description: The amount of memory used by the OS page cache, in bytes. Typically, almost all available memory is used by the OS page cache - high values of this metric are normal and expected. This is a system-wide metric, it includes all the processes on the host machine, not just clickhouse-server.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSMemoryFreePlusCached
metrics.description: The amount of free memory plus OS page cache memory on the host system, in bytes. This memory is available to be used by programs. The value should be very similar to `OSMemoryAvailable`. This is a system-wide metric, it includes all the processes on the host machine, not just clickhouse-server.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSMemoryFreeWithoutCached
metrics.description: The amount of free memory on the host system, in bytes. This does not include the memory used by the OS page cache memory, in bytes. The page cache memory is also available for usage by programs, so the value of this metric can be confusing. See the `OSMemoryAvailable` metric instead. For convenience we also provide the `OSMemoryFreePlusCached` metric, that should be somewhat similar to OSMemor...

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSMemorySwapCached
metrics.description: The amount of memory in swap that was also loaded in RAM. Swap should be disabled on production systems. If the value of this metric is large, it indicates a misconfiguration. This is a system-wide metric, it includes all the processes on the host machine, not just clickhouse-server.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSMemoryTotal
metrics.description: The total amount of memory on the host system, in bytes.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSNiceTimeNormalized
metrics.description: The value is similar to `OSNiceTime` but divided to the number of CPU cores to be measured in the [0..1] interval regardless of the number of cores. This allows you to average the values of this metric across multiple servers in a cluster even if the number of cores is non-uniform, and still get the average resource utilization metric.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSOpenFiles
metrics.description: The total number of opened files on the host machine. This is a system-wide metric, it includes all the processes on the host machine, not just clickhouse-server.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSProcessesBlocked
metrics.description: Number of threads blocked waiting for I/O to complete (`man procfs`). This is a system-wide metric, it includes all the processes on the host machine, not just clickhouse-server.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSProcessesCreated
metrics.description: The number of processes created. This is a system-wide metric, it includes all the processes on the host machine, not just clickhouse-server.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSProcessesRunning
metrics.description: The number of runnable (running or ready to run) threads by the operating system. This is a system-wide metric, it includes all the processes on the host machine, not just clickhouse-server.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSSoftIrqTimeNormalized

This allows you to average the values of this metric across multiple servers in a cluster even if the number of cores is non-uniform, and still get the average resource utilization metric.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSThreadsTotal

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSUptime

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.OSUserTimeNormalized

This allows you to average the values of this metric across multiple servers in a cluster even if the number of cores is non-uniform, and still get the average resource utilization metric.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.PageCacheBytes

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.PageCacheCells
metrics.description: Total number of entries in the userspace page cache.

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.PageCacheMaxBytes

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.PageCachePinnedBytes

metrics.name: clickhouse.asynchronous_metrics.ReplicasMaxInsertsInQueue

releaseNotes.notes:
***Fixed***:

* Send the `database_instance` metadata event before metric queries run, so a failing query no longer suppresses it. ([#25530](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/25530))
* Declare the accepted values of `compression` in the configuration spec. ([#25603](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/25603))
* Exclude internal resource tags from the `database_instance` metadata payload. ([#25692](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/25692))

***Fixed***:

* Log query sample obfuscation failures with repr so an embedded null cannot crash the job. ([#25344](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/25344))

***Added***:

* Add ClickHouse 26.3 support ([#24302](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24302))
* Update dependencies ([#24817](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24817))
* Add the hosting type, the connection mode and the cluster node inventory to the ``database_instance`` metadata payload. ([#24889](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24889))

***Fixed***:

* Add MarkCacheBytes to SystemMetrics query mapping for ClickHouse 25.x+ compatibility, where the metric was moved from system.asynchronous_metrics to system.metrics. ([#23677](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23677))
* Fix a crash on Altinity FIPS builds whose version string includes a non-numeric suffix (e.g. ``25.3.8.30001.altinityfips``). ([#24807](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24807))
* Fixes a duplicate query for Clickhouse server version. ([#24916](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24916))
* Fan out over the cluster the instance actually belongs to in single endpoint mode, instead of assuming it is named ``default``, and read local system tables when no cluster can be resolved. ([#24920](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24920))
* Manage the DBM async jobs through the ``DatabaseCheck`` registry. ([#24934](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24934))
* Cache the Agent version instead of resolving it for every payload. ([#25024](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/25024))

***Fixed***:

* Fix a crash on Altinity FIPS builds whose version string includes a non-numeric suffix (e.g. ``25.3.8.30001.altinityfips``). ([#24807](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24807))

***Added***:

* Update dependencies ([#24321](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24321))
* Add async insert buffer snapshot collection for DBM, piggybacked into the query samples job. ([#24517](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24517))
* Add collection of asynchronous insert flush health from ``system.asynchronous_insert_log`` for DBM. ([#24549](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24549))
* Add ClickHouse node-level data across DBM checks: a `server_node` field on query metrics, node identity on query samples, completions, and errors (`@clickhouse.clickhouse_node`), and a `clickhouse_node` tag on parts/merges and view-refresh metrics. ([#24633](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24633))
* Add a `clickhouse_cluster` tag to ClickHouse DBM metrics and events. ([#24711](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24711))
* Add a `hosting_type` tag identifying whether the ClickHouse instance is ClickHouse Cloud or self-hosted. ([#24736](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24736))

***Fixed***:

* Collect standard system table metrics per node via clusterAllReplicas in single endpoint mode so per-node counters no longer produce phantom failures (e.g. clickhouse.query.failed.count). ([#24266](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24266))
* Fixes query completions payload always reporting a null service. ([#24632](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24632))
* Standardize how the integration declares its Database Monitoring platform identifier, and bump the minimum ``datadog-checks-base`` version to 37.42.0. ([#24649](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24649))

***Added***:

* Bump the minimum supported version of `datadog-checks-base` to 37.41.0. ([#24267](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24267))

***Fixed***:

* Fix the `database_hostname` tag and metadata to always report the resolved database host instead of the `reported_hostname` override. ([#24247](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24247))
* Remove duplicated `agent_hostname` logic now provided by the `DatabaseCheck` base class. ([#24268](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24268))
* Remove duplicated tags logic now provided by the `DatabaseCheck` base class. ([#24272](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24272))
* Remove duplicated `database_identifier` logic now provided by the `DatabaseCheck` base class. ([#24276](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24276))

***Changed***:

* Update the list of supported ClickHouse versions and relevant metrics to the latest. ([#21294](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/21294))

***Added***:

* Add CPU time metrics (cpu_us, cpu_wait_us) to ClickHouse query metrics, query completions, and query errors. ([#23882](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23882))
* Add ClickHouse schema collection: catalog payload (databases, tables, views, columns) under collect_schemas with include/exclude regex filters for databases and tables. ([#23899](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23899))
* Add ClickHouse schema metrics: per-table size gauges and per-view refresh status gauges under schema_metrics. ([#23900](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23900))

***Fixed***:

* Fix ClickHouse check to honor the reported_hostname config option and fall back to the agent hostname when connecting via localhost or 127.0.0.1. ([#23756](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23756))
* Store advanced-queries metric definitions as JSON loaded on first check run. ([#23829](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23829))
* Bump `datadog-checks-base` to `>=37.39.1`. ([#23950](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23950))

***Added***:

* Add parts and merges monitoring (DBM): per-table gauges for parts, merges, mutations, and replication queue health, plus a per-cycle row-level event payload for the DBM Storage Health timeline view. ([#23361](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23361))

***Fixed***:

* Fix SSL certificate verification being ignored when `verify: false` is set. The shared connection pool was created without TLS settings, causing `verify=False` to be silently ignored when clickhouse-connect skips its own TLS pool creation for a pre-supplied pool manager. ([#23450](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23450))
* Skip emitting empty storage_health payloads when every parts-and-merges collection is empty. ([#23553](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23553))

***Added***:

* Update dependencies ([#22996](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/22996))
* Add query error collection from system.query_log for DBM ([#23041](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23041))
* Add support for ClickHouse explain plans. ([#23286](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23286))

***Fixed***:

* Bump `datadog-checks-base` to `>=37.34.1`. Notable changes:
    - Reduce allocations in `StatementMetrics` by deferring dict construction and updating the previous-statements cache in place. ([#23075](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23075)) ([#23282](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23282))

***Added***:

* Add support for security validation in models ([#23109](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23109))

***Fixed***:

* Fix authentication regression where a missing `password` config option defaults to `None` instead of an empty string, causing ClickHouse to reject connections with error code 194. ([#23015](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23015))

***Added***:

* Add ClickHouse support for DBM with Query Metrics, Query Samples, and Query Completions ([#22341](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/22341))
* Update dependencies ([#22707](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/22707))

***Fixed***:

* Fix query_signature mismatch between DBM query metrics and query samples by using raw query text instead of ClickHouse's normalizeQuery() for obfuscation ([#22831](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/22831))
